hints: A knight move changes coordinates by 1 and 2, so the board graph is unweighted.
Run breadth-first search starting at the top-left square; first reaching a square gives its shortest distance.
Explore all eight legal knight jumps and do not revisit a square already assigned a distance.
analogy: Treat each square as a room and each legal knight jump as a hallway; breadth-first search visits rooms by jump count.
example: For n=4, square (2,3) is one knight jump from (1,1), so its printed distance is 1.
algorithm: Initialize distance(1,1)=0 and push it into a queue. Repeatedly pop a square and assign distance+1 to each unvisited legal knight destination.
correctness: BFS explores all paths with d jumps before paths with d+1 jumps, so the first assigned distance is minimal.
complexity: O(n^2) time and O(n^2) space for the board.
